findings.finding: The mini-plan was written retroactively, after the work was already complete and reviewed. The document explicitly says it "exists to give the external reviewer a real approach description to review... not to gate work that is already complete." A plan that cannot gate the work it describes is not a plan; the external review of it is theater. The trigger conditions (100-LOC diff) were met before build time — the diff was known, only the re-check script hadn't run.
findings.suggestion: Own this as a process failure and fix the tooling so the diff-driven re-check runs before build (make `classify_complexity.py` or the Step-3.4 check part of the pre-build path). The retroactive document is acceptable as a correction, but the plan should name the process fix, not just the document.

findings.finding: Disposition #6 (blank-line trimming in six files) rejects the "metric gaming" finding on the grounds that the total line count is honestly unchanged. But the bloat ratchet exists to bound file growth from test backfill marker sprawl; offsetting marker lines by deleting blank separators preserves the letter of the metric while defeating its purpose (readability/structure of the test files). The disposition argues the metric is "line count" as if that's obviously the right metric — it isn't obviously, and the response reads as rationalizing.
findings.suggestion: Either accept the ratchet bump (it reflects real growth) or get an explicit ruling from the metric owner on whether blank-line-trim offsets are permitted. Don't self-adjudicate a rejected medium finding with "the count is honestly the same."

findings.finding: AC26's "recorded reason" lives in a markdown file (seam-survey Named Exception 5), not in the machine-checked artifact (`shipwright_ac_coverage_baseline.json` has no per-entry reason field — acknowledged in disposition #4). The AC says "recorded reason why no existing seam can prove it"; a prose note in a planning doc is not verifiable in CI and will drift.
findings.suggestion: Record the reason in the JSON (even as a string field on the unbound entry, or a sidecar file the ratchet script validates). If that's a schema change out of this unit's scope, note it as a follow-up task in the plan rather than declaring the markdown note sufficient.

findings.finding: AC26's unbound reason ("definitional/policy guarantee, no deterministic surface") is asserted but not argued. Many "the system explicitly does not do X" ACs can be proven — e.g., assert that triage output contains no plan-generation call, or that the docs/schema surface that claim. "No seam exists" is doing a lot of work for one of 29 ACs.
findings.suggestion: Include the actual AC26 text and the candidate seams considered in the plan, so the exception is auditable rather than a wave-off. The precedent (FR-01.12 Exception 1) should be cited with its reasoning, not just its existence.

findings.finding: The scope-note conflict (sub-iterate spec says `shared/scripts/tests`, actual roots are `shared/tests` + `shared/scripts/tools/tests`) is left uncorrected because the spec is "out of scope." Leaving a known-wrong scope line in the governing spec invites the next sub-iterate to follow it.
findings.suggestion: File the one-line spec correction as a tracked follow-up (or a trivial doc PR alongside this unit) rather than only reconciling it inside this plan document.

findings.finding: AC19's binding cites a parametrized test `test_failing_check_detail_is_capped_whatever_grows[name/branch/url]` by its parametrized IDs. If the parametrization changes, the named IDs silently stop matching; the orphan-check may or may not catch param-id drift depending on how it resolves IDs.
findings.suggestion: Confirm the orphan-binding check resolves parametrized IDs (i.e., the binding survives if a fourth param is added). If it doesn't, bind to the test function name without the param suffix.

findings.finding: The change spec says "Test root(s): shared/scripts/tests (34 files)" while the plan uses two different roots and asserts "one pytest invocation per test root" was honored — but the spec's stated root was never run. If CI or any downstream tooling reads the sub-iterate spec to determine what to run, those 34 files get no coverage signal from this unit.
findings.suggestion: Verify nothing consumes the spec's test-root line for execution; if something does, that's a real gap, not just prose.

findings.finding: The binding scope is internally inconsistent: the change specification names `shared/scripts/tests`, while the implementation runs `shared/tests` and `shared/scripts/tools/tests`. A prose reconciliation does not establish authority to substitute different test roots.
findings.suggestion: Obtain a campaign/spec-owner correction or explicit waiver that names the two executed roots, then record it in the canonical campaign artifact—not only this retroactive mini-plan.

findings.finding: AC26 remains `unbound`, while the acceptance criterion requires no cluster entry remain unbound without a recorded reason. The proposed reason is stored in a seam-survey exception rather than alongside the baseline entry, so tooling or a future reviewer cannot mechanically associate the exception with that AC.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the canonical coverage workflow can resolve `FR-01.14/AC26` to its exception deterministically (for example through an explicit exception mapping consumed by the ratchet check), and verify that this still passes after regeneration.

findings.finding: The documentation has residual evidence of copy/paste drift: verification says the tools root contains “AC08, AC25,” but the final mapping places AC08 in `shared/tests`. This weakens confidence that the claimed commands, marker locations, and per-AC accounting were revalidated after the AC08 retag.
findings.suggestion: Correct the verification record and rerun/report the root-to-AC inventory from the committed tree so each AC’s decorated test and executed root agree mechanically.

findings.finding: AC23’s observable-assertion section cites `test_is_machine_churn_requires_both_conditions`, but the per-AC mapping does not include it. If that classifier behavior is required to prove the AC, the current declared binding is incomplete; if it is not required, the narrative overstates the proof.
findings.suggestion: Add the exact decorated classifier test to the AC23 mapping, or revise the assertion explanation to rely only on the mapped tests and show they prove both clauses.

findings.finding: The plan relies on manually selected pre-existing tests and marker decorators, but does not describe a check that a single AC is not inadvertently tagged to mutually incompatible or overly broad tests. This is especially relevant for multi-clause ACs and retroactive tagging.
findings.suggestion: Add a focused audit command or review checklist that prints each FR-01.14 marker with its test body/location and validates duplicate/exceptional bindings before writing the baseline.  Overall, the test-backfill strategy is appropriate and avoids needless harnesses or production changes, but the root-scope conflict and remaining audit inconsistencies should be resolved before this can be treated as a reliable compliance backfill.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
